title: Contains Duplicate
prompt:
Given an integer array `nums`, return `true` if any value appears **at least twice**, and `false` if every element is distinct.

**Example**: `[1,2,3,1]` → `true`; `[1,2,3,4]` → `false`.
hints: Comparing every pair is O(n²). What if, as you walk the array, you remembered every value you'd already passed?
Keep a HashSet of seen values; a value that's already in it is a duplicate.
`set.add(x)` returns false if x was already present — `if (!seen.add(x)) return true;`

solution.explanation: Insight: "have I seen x before?" is an O(1) HashSet question. We add each value as we go, so the first time `add` reports the value was already present we've found a repeat; if the loop finishes, every value was distinct. O(n) time, O(n) space. Sorting and comparing neighbors is the O(n log n) time, O(1) extra space trade-off.
